title: Camp 2 close: one light, ten lamps
hookLine: Sikhs speak of one light passing through all ten Gurus, and now resting in the Granth and the Khalsa
last: THE NEEDLE — WHAT GOES WITH YOU.

cards: At a candlelight vigil, one person lights a candle, then tips it toward the next person's wick. That one lights the next, down the whole line, until the dark street is full of small flames.
And the first flame never gets smaller. Nothing is taken from it. For seventy-five days you've walked through the Sikh story, from a boy born at Talwandi to a Guru bowing before a book at Nanded.
Ten Gurus. Sikhs have one word for what connects them all, and it's the word for that flame.

teach.b: Jot: light, flame, the light of the divine. Sikhs say there were ten Gurus in body, but one light. It's in the Guru Granth Sahib itself.
Two musicians at Guru Arjan's court, Satta and Balwand, sang that the light was the same and the way was the same; only the body changed.
Nanak's light in Angad, then in Amar Das, then Ram Das, all the way to Gobind Singh. When a Guru died, Sikhs didn't say he was gone. They said his light merged back into the light.
And at Nanded the light didn't go out.

teach.h: RESTING IN THE GRANTH AND THE KHALSA.
teach.b: It came to rest in two places: the Guru Granth Sahib, and the Khalsa, the community gathered. Look back at what that light did in this camp. Sacha sauda, the true bargain of feeding the hungry.
Mardana's rebab, the travels, Kartarpur. Angad's ang, the wrestling ground, the baoli at Goindwal. The Anand, Amritsar, the four rounds of the lavan.
Harmandir Sahib, the Adi Granth, Guru Arjan's martyrdom. Miri piri and the Akal Takht. A child Guru, a Guru who gave his head in Chandni Chowk.
Vaisakhi, the Panj Pyare, amrit, the Khalsa. The Sahibzade, the Chali Mukte, the Zafarnama. Ten lamps, the same flame in every one.
And the Gurus say that flame isn't only in them.
In the evening prayer, Kirtan Sohila, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase, that in everyone there is a light, and that light is the One.
Now the next camp turns to what the light asks you to do with your hands.

how: Sikhs honor the ten Gurus as one light in ten forms, and mark each Guru's birth and passing with gurpurabs; when speaking of a Guru's death they often say he merged into the divine light.

o: the one divine light shared by all ten Gurus
a lamp lit in the gurdwara each evening
a Guru's spirit returning in a new birth

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: sang that only the body changed

s: Sikhs see the ten Gurus as ten separate teachings
Sikhs say one light passed through all ten; only the body changed.
the idea of one light is in the Guru Granth Sahib itself
Satta and Balwand sang it at Guru Arjan's court.
the Gurus taught that the light is only in them
Guru Nanak says in Kirtan Sohila that there is a light in everyone.

games.q: you're lighting candles at a vigil, one flame to the next. after you light ten others, what's happened to your own flame?
o: it has grown weaker with each one.
games.why: a flame loses nothing by lighting another. Sikhs use the picture of one light passing through ten Gurus.

practice: If you can, light a lamp or a candle somewhere safe; if not, look at any small light near you, or picture one. Watch the flame, never still, never quite the same shape twice, and yet the same flame.
Think of one person whose light reached you, a parent, a teacher, a friend: their flame lit yours, and it didn't get smaller.

wordCard.voice: Jot. The divine light, one flame through all ten Gurus, now resting in the Granth and the Khalsa. Camp two is complete.

orig.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi script: the light, as the Guru Granth Sahib spells it; everyday Punjabi writes it ਜੋਤ.

carryVoice: Your line: one light, ten lamps. Tomorrow, camp three: the practices, starting with seva. See you there.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 966 (Var of Satta and Balwand, Raag Ramkali: the same light, the same way, only the body changed)
Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 13 (Kirtan Sohila, Guru Nanak: in all is the light, and that light is the One)
